inspection_summary: All 757 logical lines were inspected. The paper exposes a reusable architecture for explicit zero-free regions: transform a positive prime-side expression with Weil's explicit formula, use trigonometric positivity and zero symmetry to discard controlled terms, split remaining zeros by geometry, bind low heights to numerical RH verification, and optimize admissible compactly supported kernels under explicit error-sign and monotonicity checks. PDF extraction preserves the prose-level mechanism and reported constants, but several displayed formulas have disrupted reading order, lost fraction bars or superscripts, and recurring 1/2→21 and π/2→π2 defects; exact formula reuse requires checking the raw PDF.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the improved zero-free-region constant, inherited method, and dependence on Platt's numerical verification.

sections_inspected.label: Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Connects zero-free regions to prime-counting error terms and identifies the explicit-formula, test-function, and numerical-verification ingredients.

sections_inspected.label: Logarithmic derivative and zeros
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Develops positivity from trigonometric averaging, isolates a candidate zero, and explains Stechkin symmetry cancellation and the explicit-formula lineage.

sections_inspected.label: Kadiri's method
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds the smoothed explicit formula, decomposes its contributions, controls zero classes and errors, and reduces the proof to an iterated scalar kernel inequality.

sections_inspected.label: Test functions and trigonometric inequalities
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Compares admissible kernel families, optimizes trigonometric weights, certifies error and monotonicity conditions, and obtains the improved constant.

sections_inspected.label: References and author information
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic provenance and non-mathematical end matter.

accepted_units.title: Zero-free geometry as an explicit prime-counting error control
accepted_units.why_material: The introduction makes the causal bridge from excluding zeros near one to an exponential error estimate for prime counting, then identifies which proof components are being changed and which numerical result is imported.
accepted_units.context_note: Keep the historical progression and theorem statement together because the claimed improvement is meaningful only relative to the prior constant and its proof interface.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The displayed Li integral and error-term formula at lines 28-39 have degraded layout; the prose and direction of dependence are recoverable, but exact typography requires the raw PDF.

accepted_units.title: Trigonometric averaging converts the Euler side into a nonnegative constraint
accepted_units.why_material: The logarithmic derivative and Hadamard-product representation are combined with a nonnegative cosine polynomial so a chosen zero can be isolated while the prime-side weighted sum remains nonnegative.
accepted_units.context_note: The classical polynomial example is retained with its surrounding logarithmic-derivative inequalities because it demonstrates the reusable mechanism rather than merely naming positivity.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Multiline sums, fractions, and powers are extraction-sensitive; the sign logic and coefficient pattern are readable, but exact formulas should be verified against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Stechkin symmetrization makes paired zero contributions discardable
accepted_units.why_material: The zero symmetries ρ̄ and 1−ρ̄ are paired with a shifted logarithmic derivative so all nonexceptional contributions have a controlled sign, improving the constant available from the raw positivity argument.
accepted_units.context_note: The lemma, symmetry pairing, shifted combination, and resulting zero-free consequence form one indivisible mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several fractions and the factor involving a square root are visually degraded, including 1/2-like terms; use the raw PDF for coefficients, while the prose-supported pairing and discard operation are reliable.

accepted_units.title: A compactly supported test function turns Weil's formula into four controllable contribution classes
accepted_units.why_material: The source introduces an admissible test function and Laplace transform, then forms a shifted difference that decomposes the positive prime sum into archimedean, pole, zero, and remainder terms.
accepted_units.context_note: Definitions of F, D, Δ1, Δ2, T1, and T2 are kept with the resulting identity because later bounds refer to this complete decomposition.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The contour integral and transforms are split across lines and have superscript/subscript loss; exact symbolic transcription requires the PDF, but the decomposition and roles of its terms are recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Positivity parameters are rescaled around a candidate zero and anchored by verified low zeros
accepted_units.why_material: The method wraps the explicit formula in a positive trigonometric polynomial, parameterizes distance from the line Re(s)=1, and uses a finite verified-height boundary so the remaining analytic argument only addresses higher zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: The definitions of η, r, σ, ω, T0, and the positivity condition on Re(F) must remain together to expose the analytic/computational division of labor.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The extraction renders 1/2 as 21 at line 352 and disrupts several ratios; the numerical cutoff and parameter relations are prose-supported, but exact inequalities require the raw PDF.

accepted_units.title: Exceptional-zero isolation and geometric partition reduce the proof to signed error budgets
accepted_units.why_material: The candidate zero is separated, the remaining zeros are partitioned into a sign-discardable class and a density-controlled class, and four auxiliary estimates are assembled into one master inequality with a single correction term C(η).
accepted_units.context_note: Propositions 2-5 are concise citations to prior estimates, but their roles and aggregation are explicit here and constitute the reusable proof organization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The definitions of S1 and S2 include a 1/2→21 defect and dense displayed formulas; verify boundary constants and individual terms in the PDF before exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Kernel rescaling converts the master inequality into an iterative bound on the zero-free constant
accepted_units.why_material: Scaling f by η collapses the proof to a kernel functional K(ω,θ); negativity of the correction and monotonicity in ω yield a scalar inequality that can be iterated to improve R.
accepted_units.context_note: The kernel definition, monotonicity condition, numerical parameter choice, and six-step update are retained as one strategic unit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The support endpoint and explicit hθ formula are badly line-broken, so the exact kernel needs PDF verification; the rescaling, monotonicity, and iterative-bootstrap logic are clear in prose.

accepted_units.title: Test-function and trigonometric families define a constrained representation search
accepted_units.why_material: The authors vary both the smoothing kernel and the positive cosine polynomial while preserving the same proof interface, reject empirically worse polynomial forms, and update the verified-height cutoff before optimization.
accepted_units.context_note: This unit captures the experimental design rather than any one winning numerical parameter set.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Polynomial exponents and summation layout are flattened by extraction; family membership and the selected quartic form are recoverable, but exact coefficients should be checked in the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Four admissible kernels are compared under the same certification pipeline
accepted_units.why_material: Propositions 6-9 hold the analytic framework fixed while changing kernel representations, numerically maximizing their objective, rechecking admissibility, correction negativity, and monotonicity, and comparing the resulting constants.
accepted_units.context_note: The repeated proof structure is grouped into one comparative unit; splitting each proposition would mostly duplicate the same mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Kernel formulas are extraction-sensitive, π/2 is degraded at lines 536 and 619, and two proofs are omitted by the paper itself; reported parameter choices and resulting constants are readable, but exact kernel definitions require the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Autocorrelation builds an admissible kernel whose optimization gives the best bound
accepted_units.why_material: A compactly supported nonnegative even function is convolved with itself, automatically satisfying the needed endpoint and transform-positivity constraints; the same numerical certification pipeline then yields the best reported constant.
accepted_units.context_note: The construction of g, its convolution h, the parameter search, componentwise error bounds, monotonicity check, and conclusion are kept together.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The convolution limits and displayed objective are line-broken, though the construction and certification inequalities remain legible; exact integral notation and decimals should be checked against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Parameter nonuniqueness and a structurally different kernel family test representation sensitivity
accepted_units.why_material: The remarks show that nearby parameterizations reproduce the best constant while a different hyperbolic-trigonometric construction performs slightly worse, providing both robustness evidence and a negative comparison.
accepted_units.context_note: The statement that Mathematica was used is retained because the printed paper does not otherwise provide a reproducible numerical-search implementation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The alternative kernel formula is readable but typography-sensitive; exact reproduction requires the PDF and an independently specified computation.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From prime-side positivity to a scalar zero-free inequality
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The proof is a staged compression: positivity of a weighted prime sum feeds an explicit formula, symmetry removes most zero contributions, a geometric partition budgets the rest, verified low zeros close the finite range, and rescaling reduces everything to a monotone scalar kernel inequality.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Several component estimates are cited from Kadiri rather than proved here, and exact displayed formulas are extraction-sensitive.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Optimization over representations with invariant proof obligations
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Different kernels and positive trigonometric polynomials can be searched as interchangeable representations provided each candidate preserves admissibility, correction negativity, transform positivity, and monotonicity; quality is then measured by the resulting zero-free constant.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The numerical optimization is only summarized, uses Mathematica, and lacks enough implementation detail for independent reproduction from this text alone.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: A clean analytic-computational division of labor
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Finite computation certifies all zeros below a frozen height, while the analytic kernel argument controls every higher candidate and iteratively improves the global constant.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The numerical RH certificate is cited rather than embedded, so the source records dependence on verification but does not itself reproduce it.

stop_reason: Every one of the 757 logical lines was classified. The remaining unselected material consists of front matter, transitions, running headers, bibliography, cited rather than reproduced estimates, and repeated kernel trials already grouped in a comparative unit. Further splitting would chiefly duplicate the same four-step numerical certification pattern or isolate formula fragments whose extraction is too defective for independent semantic use.
